about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.

4abba57.note: The four blobs that draw a frame, sha256, read from the checkout that ran the capture. index.html plus the three js/ files that put a pixel on screen: js/10_assets.js makes the textures, js/20_level.js the lit materials, js/40_render.js is the rasterizer. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536). The session that took these pixels proved this build off the wire, blob by blob, against the deployed page.

shots.note: RE-TAKEN from the DEPLOYED page for #882 at build cc0a3e3. The previous pass bound 44ff9a4; since then #879 widened a slab’s shadow gap from a one-pixel crease into a hand-wide band and paid its luma back onto the rest of the plate (f1463d4), #880 re-pitched the joists under a raised floor from 0.50 m to 0.77 m with a narrower, deeper shadow line at the same area (7c37ac1), and #19 moved the roof’s and the deck’s detail under the sheet’s own resolution limit (a319158, 29c967f). Two of the four blobs that draw a frame — js/40_render.js and js/10_assets.js — differ between 44ff9a4 and this checkout, so recap labelled the 44ff9a4 rows FRAME-STALE and the front page was describing a picture that no longer ships. This pass is the same eight poses re-run against the deploy, which serves main’s bytes: index.html and all eleven js/ blobs served by that URL sha256-match this checkout, twelve for twelve, proved before the shutter. Route: `node tools/livecap.js frames --url <deployed ?dev=1&seed=60&boot=0> --vp 1440x763`, one page load and one boot per pose, DEV.freeze(true), DEV.set("grain",0), DEV.clear() before the pose, shutter from the canvas after DEV.tick; the pose table is checked into tools/livecap.js (FRAMES) so the eight are reproducible without a transcript, and --vp pins the display surface with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride to the 1440x763 every frame in docs/screens carries (this chromium reports innerHeight 620 for every --window-size, and livecap's capture default came back 1440x620). Chromium gave RGBA; committed through tools/png_rgb.js. Every seat, layout and audio term below was read back out of the page that drew the frame, and every mean re-measured from these bytes with tools/recap.js’s own decoder. Pose: the spawn seat, then DEV.clear() and DEV.spawn('grunt', 1, 6); the route’s own seat search needed no turn and left him dead on the view line at (11.10, 4.53), 6.00 m out, with 255 raster px of him painted. Frame mean 60.58, which is -0.18 on the frame it replaces, and 4.18% of its pixels differ from those bytes by the kept-pixel rule (summed |dRGB| over 18, counted over the whole 1440x763 frame, which is the rule tools/livecap.js states). Layout signature 4083630493 for ARCHIVE SUBLEVEL under seed 60 on this instrument — identical to the row this frame replaces, so this is a picture change and not a re-deal. Audio term: SND.ac.sampleRate read 44100 in the page that drew this frame, the same instrument term those rows state (#404).
